Generalized nonuniform dichotomies and local stable manifolds

Date: August 24, 2026
Abstract.

We establish the existence of local stable manifolds for semiflows generated by nonlinear perturbations of nonautonomous ordinary linear differential equations in Banach spaces, assuming the existence of a general type of nonuniform dichotomy for the evolution operator that contains the nonuniform exponential and polynomial dichotomies as a very particular case. The family of dichotomies considered allow situations for which the classical Lyapunov exponents are zero. Additionally, we give new examples of application of our stable manifold theorem and study the behavior of the dynamics under perturbations.

Key words and phrases: 
Invariant manifolds, nonautonomous differential equations, nonuniform generalized dichotomies
2000 Mathematics Subject Classification
37D10, 34D09, 37D25

1. Introduction

The concept of nonuniform hyperbolicity was introduced by Pesin [11, 12, 13] and generalizes the classical concept of (uniform) hyperbolicity by allowing the rates of expansion and contraction to vary from point to point. For nonuniformly hyperbolic trajectories, Pesin [11] was able to obtain a stable manifold theorem in the finite dimensional setting. Then, in [15] Ruelle gave a proof of this theorem based on the study of perturbations of products of matrices occurring in Oseledets’ multiplicative ergodic theorem [9]. Another proof, based on the classical work of Hadamard, was obtained by Pugh and Shub in [14] and uses graph transform techniques. In the infinite dimensional setting, Ruelle  [16] proved, following his approach in [15], a stable manifold theorem in Hilbert spaces under some compactness assumptions. For transformations in Banach spaces and under some compactness and invertibility assumptions, Mañé established the existence of stable manifolds in [8] and in [17] Thieullen weakened Mañé’s hypothesis.

In the context of nonautonomous differential equations, stable manifold theorems were also obtained, assuming that the evolution operator have bounds that are nonuniform, more precisely assuming that the evolution operator admits a nonuniform exponential dichotomy, a notion introduced by Barreira and Valls in [1] and inspired both in the classical notion of exponential dichotomy introduced by Perron in [10] and in the notion of nonuniformly hyperbolic trajectory introduced by Pesin in [11, 12, 13]. For more details we refer the reader to the book [2].

Recently it has been addressed the problem of obtaining stable manifolds for perturbations of linear ordinary differential equations assuming the existence of nonuniform dichotomies that are not exponential. Namely, in [6] were obtained local and global stable manifolds for polynomial dichotomies and in [4] it was proved the existence of global stable manifolds for a generalized type of dichotomy that includes both the polynomial and exponential cases. Also in [3] Barreira and Valls obtained local stable manifolds for perturbations of linear equations assuming a dichotomy that follows growth rates of the form eρ⁡(t)\e^{\rho(t)} where ρ:ℝ0+→ℝ0+\rho:\mathds{R}^{+}_{0}\to\mathds{R}^{+}_{0} is an increasing differentiable function satisfying

limt→+∞log⁡tρ⁡(t)=0.\lim_{t\to+\infty}\frac{\log t}{\rho(t)}=0. (1)

This definition, in spite of being very general, does not include some of the growth rates considered in this paper, namely, due to (1), this definition do not include for example the polynomial case studied in  [6] and the growth rates of Examples 3.4 and 3.5. In the discrete time setting, the existence of global and local stable manifolds for perturbations of some nonuniform polynomial dichotomies was discussed in [5].

The main objective of this paper is to obtain local stable manifolds for perturbations of nonautonomous linear ordinary differential equations, assuming that the evolution operator associated with the linear equation admits a dichotomy with growth rates given by increasing functions that go to infinity (and therefore more general than the mentioned above). In fact we do not need to assume condition (1) and we allow growth rates given by non-differentiable functions as well as different growth rates in the uniform and in the nonuniform parts of the dichotomy. We also would like to emphasize that the dichotomies considered here include as a particular case the ones considered in [1] and [6] and the theorems proved there, respectively, for nonuniform exponential dichotomies and for nonuniform polynomial dichotomies, are particular cases of the result presented in this paper. We also give new examples of growth rates to which our local stable manifold theorem can be applied. We emphasize that the Lyapunov exponent considered in [2], for Hilbert spaces, is zero or infinity for most of the dichotomies considered in this paper.

The content of the paper is as follows: in Section 2 we establish the setting, we define the dichotomies and we state the main theorem; in Section 3 we give examples of nonuniform (μ,ν)(\mu,\nu)-dichotomies for each differentiable growth rates in our family of growth rates and examples of growth rates that verify the conditions of the main theorem; in Section 4 we prove the main theorem; finally, in Section 5, we study how the manifolds obtained vary with the perturbations considered.

2. Main result

Let XX be a Banach space and denote by B⁡(X)B(X) the space of bounded linear operators acting on XX. Given a continuous function A:ℝ0+→B⁡(X)A\colon\mathds{R}^{+}_{0}\to B(X), we consider the initial value problem

v′=A⁡(t)​v,v⁡(s)=vsv^{\prime}=A(t)v,\ v(s)=v_{s} (2)

with s≥0s\geq 0 and vs∈Xv_{s}\in X. We assume that each solution of (2) is global and denote the evolution operator associated with (2) by T⁡(t,s)T(t,s), i.e., v⁡(t)=T⁡(t,s)​vsv(t)=T(t,s)v_{s} for t≥0t\geq 0. Note that the operator T⁡(t,s)T(t,s) is invertible (see Deimling [7, Section 1.4]).

We say that an increasing function μ:ℝ0+→[1,+∞[\mu\colon\mathds{R}^{+}_{0}\to[1,+\infty[ is a growth rate if μ⁡(0)=1\mu(0)=1 and

limt→+∞μ⁡(t)=+∞.\lim_{t\to+\infty}\mu(t)=+\infty.

Let μ\mu and ν\nu be growth rates. We say that equation (2) admits a nonuniform (μ,ν)(\mu,\nu)-dichotomy in ℝ0+\mathds{R}^{+}_{0} if, for each t≥0t\geq 0, there are projections P⁡(t)P(t) such that

P⁡(t)​T​(t,s)=T⁡(t,s)​P​(s),t,s≥0P(t)T(t,s)=T(t,s)P(s),\ t,s\geq 0

and constants D≥1D\geq 1, a<0≤ba<0\leq b and ε≥0\varepsilon\geq 0 such that, for every t≥s≥0t\geq s\geq 0,

‖T⁡(t,s)​P​(s)‖≤D​(μ⁡(t)μ⁡(s))a​ν​(s)ε,\displaystyle\|T(t,s)P(s)\|\leq D\left(\dfrac{\mu(t)}{\mu(s)}\right)^{a}\nu(s)^{\varepsilon}, (3)
‖T​(t,s)−1​Q​(t)‖≤D​(μ⁡(t)μ⁡(s))−b​ν​(t)ε,\displaystyle\|T(t,s)^{-1}Q(t)\|\leq D\left(\dfrac{\mu(t)}{\mu(s)}\right)^{-b}\nu(t)^{\varepsilon}, (4)

where Q⁡(t)=Id−P⁡(t)Q(t)=\Id-P(t) is the complementary projection. When ε=0\varepsilon=0 we say that we have a uniform (μ,ν)(\mu,\nu)-dichotomy or simply a (μ,ν)(\mu,\nu)-dichotomy.

For each t≥0t\geq 0, we define the linear subspaces

E⁡(t)=P⁡(t)​X and F⁡(t)=Q⁡(t)​X.E(t)=P(t)X\quad\text{ and }\quad F(t)=Q(t)X.

Without loss of generality, we always identify the spaces E⁡(t)×F⁡(t)E(t)\times F(t) and E⁡(t)⊕F⁡(t)E(t)\oplus F(t) as the same vector space. The unique solution of (2) can be written in the form

v⁡(t)=(U⁡(t,s)​ξ,V⁡(t,s)​η),t≥sv(t)=\left(U(t,s)\xi,V(t,s)\eta\right),\ t\geq s

where vs=(ξ,η)∈E⁡(s)×F⁡(s)v_{s}=\left(\xi,\eta\right)\in E(s)\times F(s) and

U⁡(t,s):=P⁡(t)​T​(t,s)​P​(s) and V⁡(t,s):=Q⁡(t)​T​(t,s)​Q​(s).U(t,s):=P(t)T(t,s)P(s)\quad\text{ and }\quad V(t,s):=Q(t)T(t,s)Q(s).

In this paper we are going to address the problem of obtaining stable manifolds for the nonlinear problem

v′=A⁡(t)​v+f⁡(t,v),v⁡(s)=vsv^{\prime}=A(t)v+f(t,v),\ v(s)=v_{s} (5)

when equation (2) admits a nonuniform (μ,ν)(\mu,\nu)-dichotomy and there are c>0c>0 and q>0q>0 such that the perturbations f:ℝ0+×X→Xf\colon\mathds{R}^{+}_{0}\times X\to X verify, for u,v∈Xu,v\in X and t∈ℝ0+t\in\mathds{R}_{0}^{+}, the following conditions

Theorem 2.1.

limt→+∞μ​(t)a−b​ν​(t)ε=0\lim_{t\to+\infty}\mu(t)^{a-b}\nu(t)^{\varepsilon}=0 (21)

∫0+∞μ​(r)a​q​ν​(r)ε​𝑑r​ is convergent.\int_{0}^{+\infty}\mu(r)^{aq}\nu(r)^{\varepsilon}\,dr\text{ is convergent}. (22)

β⁡(t)​ and ​μ​(t)a​β​(t)−1​ are decreasing.\beta(t)\text{ and }\mu(t)^{a}\beta(t)^{-1}\text{ are decreasing.} (24)

Ψτ​(𝒱ϕ,δC,β~)⊂𝒱ϕ,δ,β\Psi_{\tau}\left(\mathcal{V}_{\phi,\frac{\delta}{C},\tilde{\beta}}\right)\subset\mathcal{V}_{\phi,\delta,\beta} (25)

≤c​‖y−z‖​(‖y‖+‖z‖)q\displaystyle\leq c\|y-z\|\left(\|y\|+\|z\|\right)^{q}

3. Examples

We start with an example of a nonautonomous linear equation that admits a nonuniform (μ,ν)(\mu,\nu)-dichotomy with arbitrary differentiable growth rates μ\mu and ν\nu.

Example 3.1.

Let ε>0\varepsilon>0 and a<0≤ba<0\leq b. Put ω=ε/2\omega=\varepsilon/2 and let μ,ν\mu,\nu be arbitrary differentiable growth rates. The differential equation in ℝ2\mathds{R}^{2} given by

{u′=(a​μ′​(t)μ⁡(t)+ω​ν′​(t)ν⁡(t)​(cos⁡t−1)−ω​log⁡ν⁡(t)​sin⁡t)​uv′=(b​μ​(t)μ′​(t)−ω​ν′​(t)ν⁡(t)​(cos⁡t−1)+ω​log⁡ν⁡(t)​sin⁡t)​v\begin{cases}u^{\prime}=\left(\dfrac{a\mu^{\prime}(t)}{\mu(t)}+\dfrac{\omega\nu^{\prime}(t)}{\nu(t)}(\cos t-1)-\omega\log\nu(t)\sin t\right)u\\[8.53581pt] v^{\prime}=\left(\dfrac{b\mu(t)}{\mu^{\prime}(t)}-\dfrac{\omega\nu^{\prime}(t)}{\nu(t)}(\cos t-1)+\omega\log\nu(t)\sin t\right)v\end{cases} (31)

has the following evolution operator

T⁡(t,s)​(u,v)=(U⁡(t,s)​u,V⁡(t,s)​v),T(t,s)(u,v)=(U(t,s)u,V(t,s)v),

where

U⁡(t,s)=(μ⁡(t)μ⁡(s))a​eω​log⁡ν⁡(t)​(cos⁡t−1)−ω​log⁡ν⁡(s)​(cos⁡s−1),\displaystyle U(t,s)=\left(\dfrac{\mu(t)}{\mu(s)}\right)^{a}e^{\omega\log\nu(t)(\cos t-1)-\omega\log\nu(s)(\cos s-1)},
V⁡(t,s)=(μ⁡(t)μ⁡(s))b​e−ω​log⁡ν⁡(t)​(cos⁡t−1)+ω​log⁡ν⁡(s)​(cos⁡s−1).\displaystyle V(t,s)=\left(\dfrac{\mu(t)}{\mu(s)}\right)^{b}e^{-\omega\log\nu(t)(\cos t-1)+\omega\log\nu(s)(\cos s-1)}.

Using the projections P⁡(t):ℝ2→ℝ2P(t)\colon\mathds{R}^{2}\to\mathds{R}^{2} defined by P​(t)​(u,v)=(u,0)P(t)(u,v)=(u,0) we have

‖T⁡(t,s)​P​(s)‖=|U⁡(t,s)|≤(μ⁡(t)μ⁡(s))a​ν​(s)ε\displaystyle\|T(t,s)P(s)\|=\left|U(t,s)\right|\leq\left(\dfrac{\mu(t)}{\mu(s)}\right)^{a}\nu(s)^{\varepsilon}
‖T​(t,s)−1​Q​(t)‖=|V​(t,s)−1|≤(μ⁡(t)μ⁡(s))−b​ν​(t)ε\displaystyle\|T(t,s)^{-1}Q(t)\|=\left|V(t,s)^{-1}\right|\leq\left(\dfrac{\mu(t)}{\mu(s)}\right)^{-b}\nu(t)^{\varepsilon}

and thus (31) admits a (μ,ν)(\mu,\nu)-dichotomy. Moreover, if t=2​k​πt=2k\pi and s=(2​k−1)​πs=(2k-1)\pi, k∈ℕk\in\mathds{N}, then

U⁡(t,s)=(μ⁡(t)μ⁡(s))a​ν​(s)εU(t,s)=\left(\dfrac{\mu(t)}{\mu(s)}\right)^{a}\nu(s)^{\varepsilon}

and this ensures us that the nonuniform part can not be removed.

Now we will give examples of application of Theorem 2.1.

Example 3.2.

If μ⁡(t)=ν⁡(t)=et\mu(t)=\nu(t)=\e^{t}, we get the local stable manifold theorem obtained by Barreira and Valls in [1]. In fact, in this case condition (21) becomes a+ε<ba+\varepsilon<b and condition (22) becomes a​q+ε<0aq+\varepsilon<0. The function β\beta is given by

β⁡(t)=|a​·​q+ε|1/q​e−ε⁡(1+2/q)​t\beta(t)=\left|a\textperiodcentered q+\varepsilon\right|^{1/q}\e^{-\varepsilon(1+2/q)t}

which is a decreasing function and

μ⁡(t)​β​(t)−1=|a​·​q+ε|1/q​e(a+ε⁡(1+2/q))​t\mu(t)\beta(t)^{-1}=\left|a\textperiodcentered q+\varepsilon\right|^{1/q}\e^{(a+\varepsilon(1+2/q))t}

is decreasing if a+ε⁡(1+2/q)<0a+\varepsilon(1+2/q)<0.

Example 3.3.

Making μ⁡(t)=ν⁡(t)=1+t\mu(t)=\nu(t)=1+t, we get the local stable manifold theorem obtained by the present authors in [6]. In this case, condition (21) becomes a+ε<ba+\varepsilon<b and condition (22) becomes a​q+ε+1<0aq+\varepsilon+1<0. Moreover,

β⁡(t)=|a​·​q+ε+1|1/q​(1+t)−(ε⁡(1+2/q)+1/q)\beta(t)=\left|a\textperiodcentered q+\varepsilon+1\right|^{1/q}(1+t)^{-(\varepsilon(1+2/q)+1/q)}

is a decreasing function and

μ⁡(t)​β​(t)−1=|a​·​q+ε+1|1/q​(1+t)(a+ε⁡(1+2/q)+1/q)\mu(t)\beta(t)^{-1}=\left|a\textperiodcentered q+\varepsilon+1\right|^{1/q}(1+t)^{(a+\varepsilon(1+2/q)+1/q)}

is a decreasing function if a+ε⁡(1+2/q)+1/q<0a+\varepsilon(1+2/q)+1/q<0.

In the next examples, we consider new growth rates for which Theorem 2.1 holds. Recall that Example 3.1 allows us to construct an example of a differential equation whose evolution operator has a dichotomy with the growth rates given.

Example 3.5.

Let

for every r≥sr\geq s and every ξ∈Bs,δ,β\xi\in B_{s,\delta,\beta}. From (4), (21) and (22) we have

‖(Φ​ϕ)​(s,ξ)−(Φ​ψ)​(s,ξ)‖\displaystyle\|(\Phi\phi)(s,\xi)-(\Phi\psi)(s,\xi)\|
≤∫s+∞‖V​(r,s)−1‖⋅‖fxϕ,ϕ​(r,ξ)−fxψ,ψ​(r,ξ)‖​𝑑r\displaystyle\leq\int_{s}^{+\infty}\|V(r,s)^{-1}\|\cdot\|f_{x_{\phi},\phi}(r,\xi)-f_{x_{\psi},\psi}(r,\xi)\|\,dr
≤K​μ​(s)−a​q−a+b​ν​(s)ε⁡(q+1)​β​(s)q|ξ|⋅|ϕ−ψ|∫s+∞′⁡μ​(r)a​q+a−b​ν​(r)ε​𝑑r\displaystyle\leq K\mu(s)^{-aq-a+b}\nu(s)^{\varepsilon(q+1)}\beta(s)^{q}\|\xi\|\cdot\|\phi-\psi\|^{\prime}\int_{s}^{+\infty}\mu(r)^{aq+a-b}\nu(r)^{\varepsilon}\,dr
≤K​μ​(s)−a​q​ν​(s)ε⁡(q+1)​β​(s)q|ξ|⋅|ϕ−ψ|∫s+∞′⁡μ​(r)a​q​ν​(r)ε​𝑑r\displaystyle\leq K\mu(s)^{-aq}\nu(s)^{\varepsilon(q+1)}\beta(s)^{q}\|\xi\|\cdot\|\phi-\psi\|^{\prime}\int_{s}^{+\infty}\mu(r)^{aq}\nu(r)^{\varepsilon}\,dr
=K​‖ξ‖⋅‖ϕ−ψ‖′\displaystyle=K\|\xi\|\cdot\|\phi-\psi\|^{\prime}

for every s≥0s\geq 0 and every ξ∈Bs,δ,β\xi\in B_{s,\delta,\beta} and with K=2q+2​3q​c​Cq+1​D​δqK=2^{q+2}3^{q}c\,C^{q+1}D\delta^{q}. Therefore, for every ϕ,ψ∈𝒳δ,β∗\phi,\psi\in\mathcal{X}^{*}_{\delta,\beta}, we obtain

‖(Φ​ϕ)−(Φ​ψ)‖′≤2q+2​3q​c​Cq+1​D​δq​‖ϕ−ψ‖′\|(\Phi\phi)-(\Phi\psi)\|^{\prime}\leq 2^{q+2}3^{q}c\,C^{q+1}D\delta^{q}\ \|\phi-\psi\|^{\prime}

and choosing δ>0\delta>0 sufficiently small, Φ\Phi is a contraction on 𝒳δ,β∗\mathcal{X}^{*}_{\delta,\beta}.

By the Banach fixed point theorem, Φ\Phi has a unique fixed point and this fixed point verifies (46) for every s≥0s\geq 0 and every ξ∈E⁡(s)\xi\in E(s). ∎

Now the proof of Theorem 2.1 follows easily.

Proof of Theorem 2.1.

For each ϕ∈𝒳δ,β∗\phi\in\mathcal{X}^{*}_{\delta,\beta}, using Lemma 4.1, there is a unique function xϕx_{\phi} in ℬs,δ,β\mathcal{B}_{s,\delta,\beta} satisfying (33). By Lemma 4.2 solving (34) is equivalent to solve (46) and from Lemma 4.3 there is a unique solution of (46). Hence, choosing δ>0\delta>0 sufficiently small, the existence of a stable manifold is established.

Moreover, for every s≥0s\geq 0, every t≥st\geq s and every ξ,ξ¯∈Bs,δC,β~\xi,\bar{\xi}\in B_{s,\frac{\delta}{C},\tilde{\beta}}, it follows from (14) and (37) that

‖Ψt−s​(ps,ξ)−Ψt−s​(ps,ξ¯)‖\displaystyle\|\Psi_{t-s}(p_{s,\xi})-\Psi_{t-s}(p_{s,\bar{\xi}})\| =‖(t,xϕ​(t,ξ),ϕxϕ​(t,ξ))−(t,xϕ​(t,ξ¯),ϕxϕ​(t,ξ¯))‖\displaystyle=\|\left(t,x_{\phi}(t,\xi),\phi_{x_{\phi}}(t,\xi)\right)-\left(t,x_{\phi}(t,\bar{\xi}),\phi_{x_{\phi}}(t,\bar{\xi})\right)\|
≤‖xϕ​(t,ξ)−xϕ​(t,ξ¯)‖+‖ϕxϕ​(t,ξ)−ϕxϕ​(t,ξ¯)‖\displaystyle\leq\|x_{\phi}(t,\xi)-x_{\phi}(t,\bar{\xi})\|+\|\phi_{x_{\phi}}(t,\xi)-\phi_{x_{\phi}}(t,\bar{\xi})\|
≤2​‖xϕ​(t,ξ)−xϕ​(t,ξ¯)‖\displaystyle\leq 2\|x_{\phi}(t,\xi)-x_{\phi}(t,\bar{\xi})\|
≤2​C​(μ⁡(t)μ⁡(s))a​ν​(s)ε​‖ξ−ξ¯‖\displaystyle\leq 2C\left(\dfrac{\mu(t)}{\mu(s)}\right)^{a}\nu(s)^{\varepsilon}\|\xi-\bar{\xi}\|

and the theorem is proved. ∎

5. Behavior under perturbations

In this section we assume that equation (2) admits a (μ,ν)(\mu,\nu)-dichotomy for some D≥1D\geq 1, a<0≤ba<0\leq b and ε>0\varepsilon>0. Given c>0c>0 and q>0q>0, let 𝒫c,q\mathcal{P}_{c,q} be the class of all perturbations f:[0,+∞[×X→Xf\colon[0,+\infty[\times X\to X that verify conditions (6) and (7) with the given cc and qq. In 𝒫c,q\mathcal{P}_{c,q} we can define a metric by

∥f−f¯∥′=sup{‖f​(t,u)−f¯​(t,u)‖‖u‖q+1:t≥0,u∈X∖{0}},\|f-\bar{f}\|^{\prime}=\sup\left\{\dfrac{\|f(t,u)-\bar{f}(t,u)\|}{\|u\|^{q+1}}\colon t\geq 0,u\in X\setminus\left\{0\right\}\right\}, (49)

for every f,f¯∈𝒫c,qf,\bar{f}\in\mathcal{P}_{c,q}.

The purpose of this section is to see how the manifolds in Theorem 2.1 vary with the perturbations. To do this we consider two perturbation f,f¯∈𝒫c,qf,\bar{f}\in\mathcal{P}_{c,q} and the functions ϕ\phi and ϕ¯\bar{\phi} given by Theorem 2.1 when we perturbe equation (2) with ff and f¯\bar{f}, respectively, and we compare the distance between ϕ\phi and ϕ¯\bar{\phi} in the metric given by (16) with the distance between ff and f¯\bar{f} in the metric given by (49).

Theorem 5.1.

Let c>0c>0 and q>0q>0. Suppose that equation (2) admits a (μ,ν)(\mu,\nu)-dichotomy for some D≥1D\geq 1, a<0≤ba<0\leq b and ε>0\varepsilon>0 and that the hypothesis of Theorem 2.1 are satisfied. Then, choosing δ>0\delta>0 sufficiently small, there exists K>0K>0 such that

‖ϕ−ϕ¯‖′≤K​‖f−f¯‖′\|\phi-\bar{\phi}\|^{\prime}\leq K\|f-\bar{f}\|^{\prime}

for every f,f¯∈𝒫c,qf,\bar{f}\in\mathcal{P}_{c,q}, where ϕ,ϕ¯∈𝒳δ,β\phi,\bar{\phi}\in\mathcal{X}_{\delta,\beta} are the functions given by Theorem 2.1, corresponding to the perturbations ff and f¯\bar{f}, respectively.

Proof.

Let (s,ξ)∈Gδ,β(s,\xi)\in G_{\delta,\beta}. From (46) we obtain

‖ϕ⁡(s,ξ)−ϕ¯​(s,ξ)‖≤∫s+∞‖V​(r,s)−1‖⋅‖fxϕ,ϕ​(r,ξ)−f¯xϕ¯,ϕ¯​(r,ξ)‖​𝑑r,\|\phi(s,\xi)-\bar{\phi}(s,\xi)\|\leq\int_{s}^{+\infty}\|V(r,s)^{-1}\|\cdot\|f_{x_{\phi},\phi}(r,\xi)-\bar{f}_{x_{\bar{\phi}},\bar{\phi}}(r,\xi)\|\,dr, (50)

where xϕ,xϕ¯∈ℬs,δ,βx_{\phi},x_{\bar{\phi}}\in\mathcal{B}_{s,\delta,\beta} are the functions given by Lemma 4.1 associated with (f,ϕ)(f,\phi) and (f¯,ϕ¯)(\bar{f},\bar{\phi}), respectively. By (49), (18), (7), (19), (38) and (39) we have for r≥sr\geq s

‖fxϕ,ϕ​(r,ξ)−f¯xϕ¯,ϕ¯​(r,ξ)‖≤‖fxϕ,ϕ​(r,ξ)−f¯xϕ,ϕ​(r,ξ)‖+‖f¯xϕ,ϕ​(r,ξ)−f¯xϕ¯,ϕ¯​(r,ξ)‖≤3q+1​‖f−f¯‖′​‖xϕ​(r,ξ)‖q+1+3q+1​c​‖xϕ​(r,ξ)−xϕ¯​(r,ξ)‖​(‖xϕ​(r,ξ)‖+‖xϕ¯​(r,ξ)‖)q+3q​c​‖ϕ−ϕ¯‖′​‖xϕ¯​(r,ξ)‖​(‖xϕ​(r,ξ)‖+‖xϕ¯​(r,ξ)‖)q≤3q+1​Cq+1​δq​‖f−f¯‖′​‖ξ‖​(μ⁡(r)μ⁡(s))a​q+a​ν​(s)ε⁡(q+1)​β​(s)q+2q​3q+1​c​Cq​δq​‖xϕ−xϕ¯‖′​‖ξ‖​(μ⁡(r)μ⁡(s))a​q+a​ν​(s)ε⁡(q+1)​β​(s)q+2q​3q​c​Cq+1​δq​‖ϕ−ϕ¯‖′​‖ξ‖​(μ⁡(r)μ⁡(s))a​q+a​ν​(s)ε⁡(q+1)​β​(s)q\begin{split}&\|f_{x_{\phi},\phi}(r,\xi)-\bar{f}_{x_{\bar{\phi}},\bar{\phi}}(r,\xi)\|\\ &\leq\|f_{x_{\phi},\phi}(r,\xi)-\bar{f}_{x_{\phi},\phi}(r,\xi)\|+\|\bar{f}_{x_{\phi},\phi}(r,\xi)-\bar{f}_{x_{\bar{\phi}},\bar{\phi}}(r,\xi)\|\\ &\leq 3^{q+1}\|f-\bar{f}\|^{\prime}\|x_{\phi}(r,\xi)\|^{q+1}+3^{q+1}c\|x_{\phi}(r,\xi)-x_{\bar{\phi}}(r,\xi)\|(\|x_{\phi}(r,\xi)\|+\|x_{\bar{\phi}}(r,\xi)\|)^{q}\\ &\quad+3^{q}c\|\phi-\bar{\phi}\|^{\prime}\|x_{\bar{\phi}}(r,\xi)\|\left(\|x_{\phi}(r,\xi)\|+\|x_{\bar{\phi}}(r,\xi)\|\right)^{q}\\ &\leq 3^{q+1}C^{q+1}\delta^{q}\|f-\bar{f}\|^{\prime}\|\xi\|\left(\dfrac{\mu(r)}{\mu(s)}\right)^{aq+a}\nu(s)^{\varepsilon(q+1)}\beta(s)^{q}\\ &\quad+2^{q}3^{q+1}cC^{q}\delta^{q}\|x_{\phi}-x_{\bar{\phi}}\|^{\prime}\|\xi\|\left(\dfrac{\mu(r)}{\mu(s)}\right)^{aq+a}\nu(s)^{\varepsilon(q+1)}\beta(s)^{q}\\ &\quad+2^{q}3^{q}cC^{q+1}\delta^{q}\|\phi-\bar{\phi}\|^{\prime}\|\xi\|\left(\dfrac{\mu(r)}{\mu(s)}\right)^{aq+a}\nu(s)^{\varepsilon(q+1)}\beta(s)^{q}\end{split} (51)

and using (43), the last estimate, (50) and taking into account that a−b<0a-b<0, we get

‖ϕ​(s,ξ)−ϕ¯​(s,ξ)‖≤3q+1​Cq+1​D​δq​‖f−f¯‖′​‖ξ‖​μ​(s)−a​q​ν​(s)ε⁡(q+1)​β​(s)q​∫s+∞μ​(r)a​q​ν​(r)ε​𝑑r+2q​3q+1​c​Cq​D​δq​‖xϕ−xϕ¯‖′|ξ|μ​(s)−a​q​ν​(s)ε⁡(q+1)​β​(s)q​∫s+∞μ​(r)a​q​ν​(r)ε​𝑑r+2q​3q​c​Cq+1​D​δq​‖ϕ−ϕ¯‖′|ξ|μ​(s)−a​q​ν​(s)ε⁡(q+1)​β​(s)q​∫s+∞μ​(r)a​q​ν​(r)ε​𝑑r≤3q+1​Cq+1​D​δq​‖f−f¯‖′​‖ξ‖+2q​3q+1​c​Cq​D​δq​‖xϕ−xϕ¯‖′​‖ξ‖+2q​3q​c​Cq+1​D​δq​‖ϕ−ϕ¯‖′​‖ξ‖.\begin{split}&\|\phi(s,\xi)-\bar{\phi}(s,\xi)\|\\ &\leq 3^{q+1}C^{q+1}D\delta^{q}\|f-\bar{f}\|^{\prime}\|\xi\|\mu(s)^{-aq}\nu(s)^{\varepsilon(q+1)}\beta(s)^{q}\int_{s}^{+\infty}\mu(r)^{aq}\nu(r)^{\varepsilon}\,dr\\ &\quad+2^{q}3^{q+1}cC^{q}D\delta^{q}\|x_{\phi}-x_{\bar{\phi}}\|^{\prime}\|\xi\|\mu(s)^{-aq}\nu(s)^{\varepsilon(q+1)}\beta(s)^{q}\int_{s}^{+\infty}\mu(r)^{aq}\nu(r)^{\varepsilon}\,dr\\ &\quad+2^{q}3^{q}cC^{q+1}D\delta^{q}\|\phi-\bar{\phi}\|^{\prime}\|\xi\|\mu(s)^{-aq}\nu(s)^{\varepsilon(q+1)}\beta(s)^{q}\int_{s}^{+\infty}\mu(r)^{aq}\nu(r)^{\varepsilon}\,dr\\ &\leq 3^{q+1}C^{q+1}D\delta^{q}\|f-\bar{f}\|^{\prime}\|\xi\|+2^{q}3^{q+1}cC^{q}D\delta^{q}\|x_{\phi}-x_{\bar{\phi}}\|^{\prime}\|\xi\|\\ &\quad+2^{q}3^{q}cC^{q+1}D\delta^{q}\|\phi-\bar{\phi}\|^{\prime}\|\xi\|.\end{split} (52)

Now, we will estimate ‖xϕ−xϕ¯‖′\|x_{\phi}-x_{\bar{\phi}}\|^{\prime}. By (33),  (51) and (3) we obtain for every t≥st\geq s

(μ⁡(t)μ⁡(s))−a​ν​(s)−ε​‖xϕ​(t,ξ)−xϕ¯​(t,ξ)‖≤(μ⁡(t)μ⁡(s))−a​ν​(s)−ε​∫st‖U⁡(t,r)‖⋅‖fxϕ,ϕ​(r,ξ)−f¯xϕ¯,ϕ¯​(r,ξ)‖​𝑑r≤3q+1​Cq+1​D​δq​‖f−f¯‖′​‖ξ‖​μ​(s)−a​q​ν​(s)ε​q​β​(s)q​∫stμ​(r)a​q​ν​(r)ε​𝑑r+2q​3q+1​c​Cq​D​δq​‖xϕ−xϕ¯‖′|ξ|μ​(s)−a​q​ν​(s)ε​q​β​(s)q​∫stμ​(r)a​q​ν​(r)ε​𝑑r+2q​3q​c​Cq+1​D​δq​‖ϕ−ϕ¯‖′|ξ|μ​(s)−a​q​ν​(s)ε​q​β​(s)q​∫stμ​(r)a​q​ν​(r)ε​𝑑r≤3q+1​Cq+1​D​δq​‖f−f¯‖′​‖ξ‖+2q​3q+1​c​Cq​D​δq​‖xϕ−xϕ¯‖′​‖ξ‖+2q​3q​c​Cq+1​D​δq​‖ϕ−ϕ¯‖′​‖ξ‖\begin{split}&\left(\dfrac{\mu(t)}{\mu(s)}\right)^{-a}\nu(s)^{-\varepsilon}\|x_{\phi}(t,\xi)-x_{\bar{\phi}}(t,\xi)\|\\ &\leq\left(\dfrac{\mu(t)}{\mu(s)}\right)^{-a}\nu(s)^{-\varepsilon}\int_{s}^{t}\|U(t,r)\|\cdot\|f_{x_{\phi},\phi}(r,\xi)-\bar{f}_{x_{\bar{\phi}},\bar{\phi}}(r,\xi)\|\,dr\\ &\leq 3^{q+1}C^{q+1}D\delta^{q}\|f-\bar{f}\|^{\prime}\|\xi\|\mu(s)^{-aq}\nu(s)^{\varepsilon q}\beta(s)^{q}\int_{s}^{t}\mu(r)^{aq}\nu(r)^{\varepsilon}\,dr\\ &\quad+2^{q}3^{q+1}cC^{q}D\delta^{q}\|x_{\phi}-x_{\bar{\phi}}\|^{\prime}\|\xi\|\mu(s)^{-aq}\nu(s)^{\varepsilon q}\beta(s)^{q}\int_{s}^{t}\mu(r)^{aq}\nu(r)^{\varepsilon}\,dr\\ &\quad+2^{q}3^{q}cC^{q+1}D\delta^{q}\|\phi-\bar{\phi}\|^{\prime}\|\xi\|\mu(s)^{-aq}\nu(s)^{\varepsilon q}\beta(s)^{q}\int_{s}^{t}\mu(r)^{aq}\nu(r)^{\varepsilon}\,dr\\ &\leq 3^{q+1}C^{q+1}D\delta^{q}\|f-\bar{f}\|^{\prime}\|\xi\|+2^{q}3^{q+1}cC^{q}D\delta^{q}\|x_{\phi}-x_{\bar{\phi}}\|^{\prime}\|\xi\|\\ &\quad+2^{q}3^{q}cC^{q+1}D\delta^{q}\|\phi-\bar{\phi}\|^{\prime}\|\xi\|\end{split}

and using (43) this implies that

‖xϕ−xϕ¯‖′≤3q+1​Cq+1​D​δq​‖f−f¯‖′+2q​3q+1​c​Cq​D​δq​‖xϕ−xϕ¯‖′+2q​3q​c​Cq+1​D​δq​‖ϕ−ϕ¯‖′.\begin{split}&\|x_{\phi}-x_{\bar{\phi}}\|^{\prime}\\ &\leq 3^{q+1}C^{q+1}D\delta^{q}\|f-\bar{f}\|^{\prime}+2^{q}3^{q+1}cC^{q}D\delta^{q}\|x_{\phi}-x_{\bar{\phi}}\|^{\prime}+2^{q}3^{q}cC^{q+1}D\delta^{q}\|\phi-\bar{\phi}\|^{\prime}.\end{split}

Thus, for δ>0\delta>0 such that 2q​3q+1​c​Cq​D​δq<1/22^{q}3^{q+1}cC^{q}D\delta^{q}<1/2 we have

‖xϕ−xϕ¯‖′≤2⋅3q+1​Cq+1​D​δq​‖f−f¯‖′+2q+1​3q​c​Cq+1​D​δq​‖ϕ−ϕ¯‖′.\|x_{\phi}-x_{\bar{\phi}}\|^{\prime}\leq 2\cdot 3^{q+1}C^{q+1}D\delta^{q}\|f-\bar{f}\|^{\prime}+2^{q+1}3^{q}cC^{q+1}D\delta^{q}\|\phi-\bar{\phi}\|^{\prime}.

It follows from the last estimate, (52) and 2q​3q+1​c​Cq​D​δq<1/22^{q}3^{q+1}cC^{q}D\delta^{q}<1/2 that

‖ϕ⁡(s,ξ)−ϕ¯​(s,ξ)‖′≤2⋅3q+1​Cq+1​D​δq​‖f−f¯‖′​‖ξ‖+2q+1​3q​c​Cq+1​D​δq​‖ϕ−ϕ¯‖′​‖ξ‖\|\phi(s,\xi)-\bar{\phi}(s,\xi)\|^{\prime}\leq 2\cdot 3^{q+1}C^{q+1}D\delta^{q}\|f-\bar{f}\|^{\prime}\|\xi\|+2^{q+1}3^{q}cC^{q+1}D\delta^{q}\|\phi-\bar{\phi}\|^{\prime}\|\xi\|

for every (s,ξ)∈Gδ,β(s,\xi)\in G_{\delta,\beta}. Hence we get

‖ϕ−ϕ¯‖′≤2⋅3q+1​Cq+1​D​δq​‖f−f¯‖′+2q+1​3q​c​Cq+1​D​δq​‖ϕ−ϕ¯‖′\|\phi-\bar{\phi}\|^{\prime}\leq 2\cdot 3^{q+1}C^{q+1}D\delta^{q}\|f-\bar{f}\|^{\prime}+2^{q+1}3^{q}cC^{q+1}D\delta^{q}\|\phi-\bar{\phi}\|^{\prime}

and if we choose δ>0\delta>0 sufficiently small such that 2q+1​3q​c​Cq+1​D​δq<1/22^{q+1}3^{q}cC^{q+1}D\delta^{q}<1/2 we obtain

‖ϕ−ϕ¯‖′≤4⋅3q+1​Cq+1​D​δq​‖f−f¯‖′\|\phi-\bar{\phi}\|^{\prime}\leq 4\cdot 3^{q+1}C^{q+1}D\delta^{q}\|f-\bar{f}\|^{\prime}

and this proves the theorem. ∎
